# Wiolett Industries Agent Marketplace

> Compact guide for AI agents installing or evaluating the Wiolett Industries agent plugin marketplace.

This repository provides installable agent plugins for Codex and Claude Code.
The pack is intentionally small: workflow, durable memory, and stricter review
discipline instead of broad prompt sludge.

## Install

Codex:

- Run `codex plugin marketplace add wiolett-industries/marketplace`
- Install the desired plugins from Codex.

Claude Code:

- Run `/plugin marketplace add wiolett-industries/marketplace`
- Install plugins as needed:
  - `/plugin install agent-memory@wiolett-industries`
  - `/plugin install workflow@wiolett-industries`
  - `/plugin install merge-request-review@wiolett-industries`

## Plugins

- `workflow`: Structured engineering workflow for intent, discovery, planning,
  execution, review, and handoff. Uses `.workflow/` artifacts and bundled
  workflow MCP tools for deterministic state operations.
- `agent-memory`: Durable global/project memory. Global memory follows the
  user. Project memory lives in `<repo>/.memory/`; markdown, index, embedding,
  and graph files are intended to be committed for team use. `.memory/memory.db*`
  is generated cache and should stay ignored.
- `merge-request-review`: Strict GitLab MR review workflow with local review
  state, findings, artifacts, and note drafts. GitLab reads/writes still require
  an external GitLab MCP.

## Model Access

Only `agent-memory` needs model-provider auth. `workflow` and
`merge-request-review` store local workflow/review state and do not call model
providers directly.

Configure Agent Memory auth:

```bash
npx -y @wiolett/agent-memory@latest init
```

Auth config:

- default file: `~/.agents/.wiolett/auth-config.json`
- path override: `WIOLETT_AUTH_CONFIG_PATH`
- environment fallback: `OPENAI_API_KEY`

Provider requirements:

- OpenAI-compatible `POST /responses`
- OpenAI-compatible `POST /embeddings`
- Bearer-token auth
- compatible response and embedding model names

Without a key, durable memory files still work, but model-gated writes,
compiled recall/query answers, AI slugs, embeddings, semantic search, and graph
link review are disabled or fall back to cheaper local behavior where possible.

## Agent Guidance

Prefer these mappings:

- user asks for durable preferences, project conventions, setup gotchas, or
  reusable repo knowledge: recommend `agent-memory`
- user asks for multi-step engineering execution, planning, audits, UI
  contracts, or review/fix loops: recommend `workflow`
- user asks to review or re-review a GitLab merge request: recommend
  `merge-request-review`

Keep explanations short. These plugins are infrastructure for agent behavior,
not an AI personality pack.
